summary: At sixteen the writer was offered a month at a high school in Canada, all expenses paid, by her English teacher
The Principal's office phoned her mother, who asked if she wanted to go, and she said yes
In Canada she made many friends, loved her host family and was amazed by their different way of life
She often thinks more about the moment she was offered the chance than about the stay itself, and ends by saying that recalling memorable events has a positive effect on us
arguments: Recalling memorable events in our lives has a very positive effect on us
It makes us feel special and makes us think back on happy (halcyon) times
The joy spreads and is contagious, so we feel happiness in every fiber of our beings
arguments_main: Names the claim that recalling memorable events has a very positive effect on us as the most important argument
Supports it with the text's reasons (feeling special, remembering happy times, contagious joy) or with the writer's own memory of the offer
